title: Oven BBQ Chicken Drumsticks with Potato Wedges
subtitle: sticky homemade barbecue-glazed drumsticks and crispy seasoned wedges, all from the oven
imageAlt: Glossy barbecue chicken drumsticks beside golden potato wedges on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Oven at 220°C (425°F) with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Line 2 rimmed baking sheets with foil; the glaze is sticky.

items.name: russet potatoes
items.note: about 4, scrubbed and cut in 8 wedges each

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Pat the drumsticks dry and toss with the oil, 1½ tsp paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Spread on one sheet.

steps.title: Season the wedges
steps.text: Toss the potato wedges with the oil, garlic powder and salt and spread cut side down on the second sheet.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast both sheets 30 minutes, turning the drumsticks and wedges once and switching the sheets halfway.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Meanwhile, simmer the ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar, Worcestershire and ½ tsp paprika in a small pot 3–4 minutes until slightly thick.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.text: Brush the drumsticks with half the glaze and roast 8 minutes; brush with the rest and roast 5–8 minutes more, until sticky and the thickest drumstick reads 74°C (165°F) near (not touching) the bone. The wedges finish at the same time.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest the chicken 5 minutes and serve with the wedges.

fixIt.fix: Brush it on only in the last 15 minutes; sugar burns if it goes on at the start.
Spread them out with space between, cut side down, and roast a few minutes longer on the upper rack.
Pink near the bone can be normal in drumsticks; trust the thermometer. 74°C (165°F) is safe; 80–85°C is more tender.

saleTip: Drumsticks are one of the cheapest cuts at No Frills, often about $7/kg in family packs.
swap: Bone-in thighs: same time and temperature, skin side up.
leftovers: Cold BBQ drumsticks are a great lunch; reheat the wedges in the air fryer.
doneness: 74°C (165°F) in the thickest drumstick, not touching the bone (Health Canada, poultry pieces). Even more tender at 80–85°C.
source: Based on tested oven-baked barbecue drumstick methods (Canadian Living, Food Network Canada): seasoned drumsticks roasted at 220°C, glazed with a homemade ketchup-brown sugar sauce for the last 15 minutes.
prepAhead: Make the glaze up to 1 week ahead; keep it in a jar in the fridge.
Season the drumsticks the night before.
reheat: At 200°C (400°F) 12–15 minutes, or in the air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 8 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: No onion powder on the chicken, and a simple ketchup, brown sugar and vinegar glaze.

stepNotes.4: Basic: ketchup, brown sugar and vinegar only.

fancy.note: A honey-butter corn on the cob alongside.

addSteps.title: Fancy side
addSteps.text: Boil the corn 5–7 minutes until tender. Brush with the melted butter stirred with the honey, and sprinkle with a pinch of salt.

why.0-0: Drumsticks have lots of connective tissue, so they stay juicy at high heat.
why.1-1: Brown sugar caramelises in the oven into a sticky glaze.
why.2-0: Russets have a dry, starchy flesh that roasts fluffy inside and crisp outside.

funFact: Barbecue sauce as a bottled product dates to 1909, but ketchup-based sauces have been home staples since the 1800s.

keeps.note: freeze the chicken; the wedges go mealy
